title: Prospective Model Fragility Index and Field Probe Slate
creator: Riley Thompson
description: Goal: produce a reproducible, ranked 'Fragility Index' for candidate open and commercial models and a prioritized 6-week field probe slate that validates fragility signals under realistic customer workloads. Motivation: customers choose Redwood for predictable inference; when upstream model availability/performance shifts we need a defensible, operationalized rubric and a small-run experiment program to validate fallback decisions before large-scale rollouts. Scope: define fragility signals, ingest telemetry + public signal sources, build a lightweight scoring pipeline, run 8 field probes across embeddings, short-chat, and long-context summarization workloads, and deliver a playbook for automated fallback triggers and procurement recommendations.
tasks: Finalize fragility signal taxonomy (latency variance, quant tolerance, regional availability, rate limit susceptibility, license churn)
Define scoring rules and weighting with Product/Research consensus
Prototype scoring pipeline using historical Redwood telemetry and synthetic workload generator
Design and schedule 8 field probes (2 embedding, 3 chat, 3 long-context) with partner customers/internal staging
Instrument dashboards for signal heatmap and probe results
Write playbook: fallback decision thresholds, procurement triage, canary roll procedures
Run post-probe retro and update scoring weights
acceptance_criteria: Fragility Index implementation with reproducible score for at least 12 candidate models
Heatmap dashboard with time-series for each signal and ability to filter by region and workload
Completed field probes with documented outcomes for each workload type
Fallback playbook signed off by Eng and Solutions leads and integration checklist for rollout automation
Recommendations for 3 model variants to add to the fallback catalog with cost/latency tradeoffs
